response.query: What staged deployment pathway (sandbox → shadow → limited deployment) and specific fidelity-monitor thresholds should be required before any live-EHR integration?
response.answer: Before live EHR integration, staged deployment through sandbox, shadow, and limited deployment is required. Fidelity-monitor thresholds for performance, data accuracy, and user impact must be met. Final approval for live integration is based on successful completion of all stages.

results.title: Integration Lifecycle Management: Best practices for integration deployment – Celigo
results.content: Celigo’s Integration Lifecycle Management simplifies the deployment process, offering tools that ensure integrations are developed, tested, and deployed with minimal risk. This guide covers best practices for deployment using ILM, focusing on sandbox testing, cloning integrations to production, and the pull/merge process, which includes the ability to ignore specific resource fields when necessary. From creating backups to testing in sandbox environments and seamlessly deploying to production, ILM helps ensure smooth transitions between development and live environments. For example, say you want to integrate Salesforce and NetSuite to sync “Accounts” and “Opportunities.” With ILM, you can build, test, and deploy this integration without risking disruption to your current production systems. In an ideal workflow, create and test integrations in a sandbox environment to fully vet updates before introducing them to production. This approach ensures that all changes are vetted and tested before they affect the live production environment, minimizing potential disruptions. After successfully testing your integration in the sandbox, the next step is to clone and deploy the tested integration to the production environment. * **Clone your tested integration to production:** Once your integration has passed sandbox testing, clone it directly into your production environment. Cloning from sandbox to production streamlines the deployment process, reducing errors and ensuring consistency between the two environments. One of ILM’s key features is the pull and merge process, which allows you to transfer changes from your sandbox into the production environment. To make further changes or enhancements to an integration, it’s best practice to implement and test modifications in a sandbox environment before deploying them to production. After you’ve completed testing in the sandbox and are ready to deploy to production, use ILM’s “create pull” feature to bring changes from the sandbox into your live system. Before merging the changes into production, ILM allows you to review every change brought over from the sandbox. Following this structured pull and merge process, you will maintain full control over which changes are deployed to production and can prevent unintended overwrites of sensitive fields. * **Practicing lifecycle management** – This guide offers insights into using ILM to manage integration lifecycles, covering scenarios for stable state rollbacks, testing, and managing integration development across teams.

results.title: VA reforming EHR deployment following 12-week review | FedScoop
results.content: The votes are in for the 2025 FedScoop. # VA reforming EHR deployment following 12-week review. The VA plans to make several major changes to how it rolls out its $16 billion electronic health records modernization program. The Department of Veterans Affairs will restructure how it implements its electronic health records modernization program following a 12-week strategic review of the $16 billion program, Secretary Denis McDonough told lawmakers Wednesday. The secretary said the continued rollout of the EHR across the nation would be dependent on testing and the ability for the facilities to make progress on deploying the system, rather than based on their location as was the initial plan. Specifically, VA will pursue technical-only (“sandbox”) deployment of Cerner technology at previously planned sites in Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISNs) 10 and 20 – ensuring technical readiness without affecting veterans or frontline clinical employees,” McDonough said in his prepared opening statement. The VA’s EHR system is eventually supposed to seamlessly connect with the DOD’s MHS Genesis modernization program. “However, gaps remain in our ability to govern and manage data between the two EHRs and with DOD to ensure seamless veteran and employee-centric information sharing and provision of managed, trusted data,” he said, adding that a clinician told him that most of the data integration happens in workers’ heads, not on the computer systems they use. By the end of the year, the VA will also publish a data strategy specific to making EHR data more interoperable, McDonough revealed. 1. ### Federal software buying bill is back in play in the House. ### VA leader eyes ‘aggressive deployment’ of AI as watchdog warns of challenges to get there. ### VA facilities faced ‘technology barriers’ in importing medical records, watchdog finds. ### VA secretary pledges progress on EHR rollout amid major workforce cuts. ### Trump budget offers big increase to VA’s EHR effort, cuts to agency IT systems. ### VA to complete EHR deployment at nine more facilities. ### VA seeks information on AI governance framework. #### Ahead of the World Cup and Olympics, DHS offers grants for counter-drone tech. ### Defense. * Starlink outage impacted Starshield, its defense communications service. ### Cyber. ### FedScoop TV.

results.title: Shadow Mode Deployment for ML Model Testing - ML Journey
results.content: # Shadow Mode Deployment for ML Model Testing. This is where shadow mode deployment emerges as a critical strategy for ML model testing, offering a sophisticated approach to validate model performance without exposing end users to potential issues. Shadow mode deployment represents a paradigm shift in how organizations approach model testing and validation. By running new models alongside existing production systems without affecting user-facing results, teams can gather comprehensive performance data, identify potential issues, and make informed decisions about full deployment rollouts. Shadow mode deployment is a testing methodology where a new machine learning model runs in parallel with the current production model, processing the same real-world data inputs but without its predictions being served to end users. Unlike testing environments that rely on historical data or synthetic datasets, shadow mode deployment provides insights into how models perform with current, real-world data. Effective shadow mode deployment requires sophisticated data flow management to ensure both models receive identical inputs. Before implementing shadow mode deployment, establish specific metrics and thresholds that determine model readiness for production. Shadow mode deployment integrates seamlessly with CI/CD pipelines, enabling automated testing workflows that can validate model performance as part of standard deployment processes. Banks and financial institutions employ shadow mode deployment to test new fraud detection and risk assessment models. Healthcare organizations use shadow mode deployment to validate diagnostic and treatment recommendation models, ensuring new AI systems meet stringent accuracy and safety requirements before affecting patient care. Successful shadow mode deployment requires tracking multiple KPIs including prediction accuracy, model latency, resource utilization, and business impact metrics. Organizations should also consider the growing importance of model explainability and fairness testing within shadow mode deployment frameworks. As regulatory requirements for AI systems increase, shadow mode testing must expand beyond performance metrics to include bias detection and ethical AI validation. Shadow mode deployment for ML model testing represents a mature, risk-averse approach to model validation that enables organizations to maintain high service quality while continuously improving their machine learning capabilities. By implementing comprehensive shadow testing strategies, teams can confidently deploy new models knowing they have been thoroughly validated against real-world conditions. Success with shadow mode deployment requires careful planning, robust infrastructure, and commitment to comprehensive testing methodologies.

results.title: What is a Shadow Deployment? - DevOps.com
results.content: What is a Shadow Deployment? # What is a Shadow Deployment? Shadow deployment, at its core, is a software deployment practice where any changes to a software application are deployed in a parallel environment that mimics the production environment. The primary purpose of shadow deployment is to test real-world application behavior under load, identify performance bottlenecks, and ensure that the application changes don’t affect the user experience negatively. It allows developers to test changes in an environment that closely replicates the live production environment, thereby reducing the risk of unforeseen issues cropping up post-deployment. With shadow deployment, the risk of such disruptions is significantly reduced as the changes are first deployed in a parallel environment. If any critical issue is identified during the shadow deployment, the changes can be rolled back without affecting the live environment. Another significant advantage of shadow deployment is that it allows for real-world testing. However, in shadow deployment, the parallel environment mirrors the live environment, ensuring testing is done under real-world conditions. Shadow deployment enables developers to test the scalability of their changes in a real-world environment, thereby ensuring efficient scaling. This ensures that when the changes are finally deployed to production, the application can efficiently scale based on user demand. One of the primary use cases of shadow deployment is performance testing. The insights gained from this testing can be used to optimize the changes, ensuring optimal performance when deployed to production. Shadow deployment allows for the testing of the migrated application in a parallel environment, ensuring that any issues are identified and rectified before the migration is made live. It allows developers to test if their changes are compatible with the dependent services, ensuring smooth interoperability when deployed to production. Finally, shadow deployment can be used to test new plugins or extensions. Shadow deployment allows for the testing of these plugins and extensions in a parallel environment, ensuring that they work as expected when deployed to production. When a new version of the application is ready, it’s deployed to the idle environment, tested and, once everything is confirmed to be working, traffic is switched from the blue to the green environment.
